content.content: ذَهَبَ • (ḏahaba) I (non-past يَذْهَبُ (yaḏhabu), verbal noun ذَهَاب (ḏahāb) or مَذْهَب (maḏhab))

content: to go away, to leave, to depart
to perish, to die, to be destroyed
to abduct, to steal, to sweep away, to annihilate
to lead someone, to conduct someone, to take someone along
to think, to believe, to hold the view, to be of the opinion

content.content: فأمّا الْبَرِيد ففيه خلاف وذهب قوم إلى أنه بالبادية اثنا عشر ميلا وبالشام وخراسان ستة أميال
About the postal route there is disagreement. Folks believed that in the desert it is twelve miles and in Syria and Khorasan six miles.

content: to escape, to slip, to lose sight of, to be forgotten
to ignore, to skip, to omit
to prepare to, to be about to

content.content: ذَهَّبَ • (ḏahhaba) II (non-past يُذَهِّبُ (yuḏahhibu), verbal noun تَذْهِيب (taḏhīb))
A Central Semitic innovation. Cognate with Hebrew זָהָב (zāhāḇ), Classical Syriac ܕܗܒܐ (dahbā), Old South Arabian 𐩹𐩠𐩨 (ḏhb).

content: letter, note, paper, piece of writing, message
the Scripture, the Qur'an or the Bible
a traditional school for teaching Qur'an

content.content: جَمِيل • (jamīl) (feminine جَمِيلَة (jamīla), masculine plural جَمِيلُون (jamīlūn) or جُمَلَاء (jumalāʔ), feminine plural جَمِيلَات (jamīlāt) or جَمَائِل (jamāʔil), elative أَجْمَل (ʔajmal))
I visited a beautiful and stunning place on my trip

أَيُّهَٰذَا الشَّاكِي وَمَا بِكَ دَاءٌ
كُنْ جَمِيلًا تَرَ الْوُجُودَ جَمِيلًا
ʔayyuhāḏā š-šākī wamā bika dāʔun

O! who be this complainant, and what is thine ailment?
Be courteous [thyself! and] thou shall see a beautiful existence.
a. 1957, Elia Abu Madi (also known as Īlya bin Ḍāhir Abū Māḍi, and as Elia D. Madey; 1890-1957)

content: a male given name, Jamil and Jameel, feminine equivalent جَمِيلَة (jamīla)

content.content:
كَتَبَ • (kataba) I (non-past يَكْتُبُ (yaktubu), verbal noun كِتَابَة (kitāba) or كَتْب (katb) or كِتَاب (kitāb))
(transitive)
From Proto-West Semitic *katab-, but the sense "to write" has long been considered a borrowing from another Central Semitic language, perhaps denominally from كِتَاب (kitāb).

content: to mark (symbols, shapes, graphs, glyphs, letters, and the like) on a surface, to write, to inscribe
to produce or generate by writing
to write up, to compose, to draw up, to draft
to set down figures with a typewriter or a keyboard, to typewrite or keyboard, to type
to put down in writing, to write down; to record; to register; to track

content.content: وَٱللَّهُ يَكْتُبُ مَا يُبَيِّتُونَ فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ

content: what they scheme by night; so turn away from them and rely upon Allah.
to write down (an event, such as a destiny or a fatality); to destine or predestine; to foreordain
Say "Never will we be struck except by what Allah
to write down (an ordinance, a law, a commandment, or the like); to prescribe

content.content: كَتَّبَ • (kattaba) II (non-past يُكَتِّبُ (yukattibu), verbal noun تَكْتِيب (taktīb))

content: to cause to write, to make someone write

content.content: طَالِب • (ṭālib) m (plural طَالِبُون (ṭālibūn) or طَلَبَة (ṭalaba) or طُلَّاب (ṭullāb), feminine طَالِبَة (ṭāliba))
Derived from the active participle of طَلَبَ (ṭalaba).
طَالَبَ • (ṭālaba) III (non-past يُطَالِبُ (yuṭālibu), verbal noun مُطَالَبَة (muṭālaba) or طِلَاب (ṭilāb))

content: to request, to demand, to ask for

content.content: Noun of place from the verb دَرَسَ (darasa).
